subject: Setting correlation of two latent variables to 1

messages.author: bdcf17e9c28c2c9d
messages.subject: Setting correlation of two latent variables to 1
parts:
I have found how to set the correlation to 0. I have tried to set the model:
model <-'a =~x1+x2+x3
     b=~x4+x5+x6
     c=~x7+x8+x9
     d=~x10+x11+x12
     a~~1*b'
cfa(model, data=xxx,estimator = "MLM",std.lv=TRUE)

I am getting the following error:
covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite.

What is wrong?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Setting correlation of two latent variables to 1
parts:
I am getting the following error:
covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite.

No, that is a warning.  Your model was still estimated.

What is wrong?

NPD matrices have linear dependencies or impossible values.  Sometimes, model parameters imply something that cannot occur in reality (e.g., negative variances or correlations that exceed 1), which is called a "Heywood case".  But your case is probably just the linear dependence that follows from 1 latent variables being perfectly correlated (because you fixed a~~b to 1). This is what you wanted to do, so ignore the warning.  

FYI, that constraint would also imply that a~~c == b~~c and that a~~d == b~~d (because a and b are the same variable), so you should label your parameters and impose those equality constraints as well, if you are testing a hypothesis of redundancy.
